Erc20Interface.description: Which ERC-20 view functions the bytecode exposes, from its selectors.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable code — one of the closed set in the documentation
(`bad_request`, `not_found`, `chain_not_supported`, `method_not_allowed`,
`uri_too_long`, `block_not_available`, `portfolio_too_large`, `token_not_covered`,
`balance_not_available`, `service_unavailable`, `internal_error`). Branch on this
and on `details.reason`, never on the sentence.

details.description:
Present only when the refusal carries something to act on: `reason` (a stable
sub-code), the bound that was hit and the actual value. Absent otherwise.

message.description:
Human-readable explanation. Numbers a client must act on are also given in
`details`; do not parse them out of this sentence, it may be reworded.

requestId.description:
The request's id, echoed from the `X-Request-Id` header. Quote it when asking for
support: it identifies this exact call. Absent only when the request did not carry
one.

ErrorEnvelope.description: Error response. Every refusal, whichever layer raises it, has this shape.

error.description:
What was refused and why: a stable `code`, a human-readable `message`, and `details`
with the numbers to act on where there are any.

EventArgumentValueState.description:
Why a decoded event argument carries no `value`. `withheld_for_size`: the value is too
large to include — the readings of one event are bounded in size, and a value that does
not fit is not given (the log's own `data` carries its bytes). Absent when `value` is given.

EventDataState.description:
Why an event log carries no `data`. `withheld_for_size`: the data is longer than one
page can carry (more than 49 151 bytes); `dataLength` gives its length in bytes, and the
topics and the decoding are still given. Absent when `data` is given.

EventDecodeErrorKind.description:
Why the decoding of a log could not run — a fault of the service, not of the log; ask
again. `seed_not_loaded`: the signature registry is not loaded yet (the service is
starting). `decoder_disabled`: decoding is switched off. `decoder_fault`: the decoder
failed on this request.

EventDecodeSearch.description:
How far an event's decoding went. `incomplete`: the decoding stopped before every
signature known for the log's hash was tried, because the work to try them on this log's
data exceeded the decoding's fixed budget — a reading given is then `ambiguous` (an
untried signature could fit too), and with no reading there is no `decodeStatus` at all.

EventLog.description: One event log emitted by a transaction, with its decoding when the signature is known.

address.description: The contract that emitted the log, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

blockNumber.description: Height of the block that includes the log.

callDepth.description: Depth of that frame, `1` = the top-level call. Present exactly when `callPath` is.

callPath.description:
The call frame that emitted the log, in the trace's encoding: the frame whose
`callPath` is this value in the transaction's trace (four hex characters per level,
the top-level call is `0000`). Stated by the transaction events method only. Absent
where the emitting frame is not known: in blocks below the first block this is
computed from (`meta.coverage.eventAttributionFromBlock`), or when no frame is
recorded for the log. Never guessed.

data.description:
The log's data, `0x`-prefixed. Absent when it is longer than 98 304 characters (more
than 49 151 bytes of data): then `dataState` is `withheld_for_size` and `dataLength`
gives its length in bytes. Never cut: a log's data is given whole or not at all. The
topics, and the decoding (which reads the whole data), are given either way.

dataLength.description: The data's length in bytes. Present exactly when `dataState` is.

dataState.description:
`withheld_for_size` when `data` is not given because it is too large to include in one
page. Absent when `data` is given.

decodeSearch.description:
`incomplete` when the decoding stopped before every signature known for this log's
hash was tried, because the work to try them on this log's data exceeded the decoding's
fixed budget. `candidateCount` then counts the fits among the signatures tried. Absent
when every known signature was tried.

decodeStatus.description:
How confident the decoding is: `verified` (one known signature, decoded), `partial`,
`ambiguous` (several known signatures fit this log, or one does but not every known
signature could be tried — `decodeSearch` is `incomplete` then; `decoded` is the best
candidate), `inferred`, `abi_missing` (signature unknown), `failed` (every known
signature was tried and none of its known layouts fits this log's topics and data —
the log is served raw, without `decoded`; or, with `errorKind`, the decoding could not
run — a fault of the service, not of the log: ask again). Absent only when
`decodeSearch` is `incomplete` and none of the signatures tried fits: nothing is
established then, and the log is not `failed`.

decoded.description: The decoded event, when the signature is known and the data decodes.

errorKind.description:
Why the decoding could not run, when it could not: a fault of the SERVICE, not of the
log (`decodeStatus` is `failed` then; ask again). Absent otherwise — a log whose known
signatures do not fit carries none.

logIndex.description: The log's index within its block.

logIndexInTx.description: The log's index within its transaction (emission order).

timestamp.description: Unix time of the block, seconds.

topics.description: The log's topics in order (`topics[0]` is the event signature hash), `0x`-prefixed.

txHash.description: Hash of the transaction that emitted the log, `0x`-prefixed.

txIndex.description: Position of the emitting transaction within its block, from `0`.

EvidenceSource.description: One evidence source a proof was read from.

sourceId.description:
Opaque identifier of the evidence source, `ev:` + 12 hex characters. Stable: the
same source carries the same identifier in every proof, so sources can be told
apart and matched across proofs.

logIndexes.description:
Positions within the transaction's receipt of the logs this frame emitted,
ascending. Empty when it emitted none.

ExecutionFrame.description:
One frame of the paged, frame-level trace: the call frame as in the summary, with its
calldata and output heads always present, plus the event logs it emitted.

FailedFrame.description: One failed call frame inside a reverted transaction.

callDepth.description:
Depth from the root frame, `1` = root: `callDepth == 1` is the transaction's own
top-level call.

callPath.description:
Position in the call tree: four hex characters per level, the root frame is
`0000`. Sort by `(callDepth, callPath)` to render the tree.

errorName.description:
Human-readable error name when the selector is known, for example `Error`. Absent
otherwise — render `revertSelector` then — and absent when the registry's name is not
an identifier (`[A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*`) of at most 128 characters; `errorSignature`
is then absent too, and is absent alone when it is not in identifier characters,
commas, parentheses and brackets of at most 512.

errorSignature.description:
Canonical signature of the error when the selector is known, for example
`Error(string)`. Absent otherwise, together with `errorName`.

revertData.description:
The revert payload, `0x`-prefixed; `0x` when the frame reverted with no data. Capped
at 4 KB: `revertDataTruncated` says when, and `revertDataLength` is the full length.

revertDataLength.description:
Full length of the revert payload in bytes, whether or not `revertData` is
truncated.

revertDataTruncated.description: `true` when `revertData` was cut at the 4 KB cap and is shorter than the payload.

revertSelector.description:
First four bytes of the revert payload, `0x`-prefixed (`0x00000000` when the
payload is shorter).

status.description: `Revert` (the frame reverted) or `Halt` (the EVM halted the frame).

FeedInternalTransfer.description:
One internal transfer: a value-carrying call frame inside a transaction. The
transaction's own top-level call is NOT one of these — it is the transaction, and it
rides the transactions feed.

blockNumber.description: Height of the block that includes the transaction.

callDepth.description:
Depth in the call tree; `1` is the transaction's own top-level call, which never
appears here.

callPath.description:
The frame's position in the call tree, as the trace encodes it — the third component
of this feed's cursor.

callType.description:
`call`, `callcode`, `create`, `create2` or `selfdestruct` — the kinds of call that
can move value; `unknown` for a kind this feed does not name.

counterparty.description: The other party of the frame, when there is one.

from.description: The frame's caller — the party the value left — lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

timestamp.description: Block time, Unix seconds.

to.description:
The frame's recipient. Absent where the trace records none — a `selfdestruct`
beneficiary is written that way when it IS the participant.

txHash.description: Hash of the transaction the frame ran in, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

txIndex.description: Position of the transaction within its block, from `0`.

valueWei.description: Value moved by this frame, in wei, as a decimal string.

FeedTokenTransfer.description: One token transfer of an address's feed.

blockNumber.description: Height of the block that includes the transfer.

eventType.description:
The log that carried it: `transfer`, `transfer_single`, `transfer_batch`, `sent`,
`minted`, `burned`, `deposit`, `withdraw`, `wrap` or `unwrap`.

from.description:
Whose balance decreased. Absent on a mint and on a `wrap` (ether wrapped into
WETH) — no token balance was debited.

logIndex.description: The log's index within its block — the position this feed pages on.

operator.description:
The party that executed an approved transfer (ERC-1155 `operator`), when the log
names one.

role.description: `sender` | `receiver` | `self` — this address's part in the transfer.

timestamp.description: Block time, Unix seconds. Absent for the same reason as `txHash`.

to.description: Whose balance increased. Absent on a burn and on an `unwrap`.

token.description:
The token that moved: its contract, standard and what the contract declares about
itself.

tokenId.description: The NFT's token id, as a decimal string.

txHash.description:
The transaction that emitted the transfer. Absent on the rare resolve miss: the
transfer is recorded by its position, and the hash is resolved alongside it.

txIndex.description: Position of the emitting transaction within its block, from `0`.

txSender.description:
Who SENT the transaction that emitted this transfer. On a batch disburser or an
approved `transferFrom` this is a different party from `from`. Absent when
unresolved — `from` never stands in for it.

txTo.description: The transaction's top-level recipient — on a router or a disburser, not the token.

value.description:
Raw amount as a decimal string, unscaled by `decimals`. Absent where the standard
carries no amount.

FeedTransaction.description:
One transaction of an address's feed: the transaction as recorded, plus how this address
took part in it.

blockNumber.description: Height of the block that includes the transaction.

counterparty.description:
The other party, when there is one. Absent on a contract creation and on a
transaction the address sent to itself: `self` already says the other side is this
address, and a null would conflate that with "no other side".

feeWei.description: Fee actually paid, in wei, as a decimal string.

gasPrice.description:
The price paid per gas, in wei, as a decimal string. Absent where it is not
available.

gasUsed.description: Gas the transaction used, from its receipt, as a decimal string.

inputSize.description: Size of the transaction's input in bytes.

methodId.description: The called function's 4-byte selector, `0x`-prefixed. Absent on a plain transfer.

methodName.description:
The function's name where the selector is known. Absent when it is not — never a
guess, and never the selector standing in for a name — and absent when the registry's
name is not an identifier (`[A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*`) of at most 128 characters.

nonce.description: The sender's nonce for this transaction.

role.description: `sender` | `receiver` | `self` — this address's part in the transaction.

status.description:
Receipt status: `1` success, `0` failure. Absent when the receipt is not yet
recorded — absence is "unknown", never "failed".

timestamp.description: Block time, Unix seconds.

to.description: The recipient. Absent on a contract creation — the contract has no `to`.

txIndex.description: Position of the transaction within its block, from `0`.

txType.description: Transaction type (0 legacy, 1 EIP-2930, 2 EIP-1559, 3 EIP-4844, 4 EIP-7702).

valueWei.description: Value moved by the top-level call, in wei, as a decimal string.

FirstSwap.description: The first swap of a new pool.

amountIn.description:
Amount sold, in whole token units (scaled by the token's decimals) as a
floating-point number — an approximation, not an exact amount. Absent where it is not
known.

amountOut.description:
Amount bought, in whole token units (scaled by the token's decimals) as a
floating-point number — an approximation, not an exact amount. Absent where it is not
known.

blockNumber.description: Block of the pool's first swap.

logIndex.description: Index of the swap event within its block.

timestamp.description: Block time, Unix seconds.

tokenIn.description:
The token sold into the pool, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed. Absent where it could not
be determined.

tokenOut.description:
The token bought from the pool, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed. Absent where it could
not be determined.

txHash.description: Hash of the transaction that made the first swap, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

FlashLoan.description: One flash loan taken inside a transaction.

amountRaw.description: The amount in the token's smallest unit, decimal string.

borrower.description:
Who received the loan, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed. Absent when the event does not
state it.

initiator.description:
Who initiated the loan, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed. Absent when the event does not
state it.

logIndex.description: The log that recorded it: its index in the block.

poolAddress.description: The contract that lent (the pool or vault emitting the flash-loan event).

protocol.description:
The lender as the index names it: `aave` (versions `v2`, `v2_amm`, `v2_arc`, `v3`),
`balancer` (`v2`), `uniswap` (`v3`, a pool's flash), `pancakeswap` (`v3`), and Aave
V2 forks under their own names — `radiant`, `aave_fork` (not Aave). Other values may
be added. Absent when the event does not state it.

protocolVersion.description: The lender's version, for example `v2` or `v3`. Absent when not stated.

tokenAddress.description: The token lent. Absent when the event does not state it.

FrameDelegation.description: Where the EIP-7702 delegation a frame ran under was set.

authIndex.description:
Position of the authorization in that transaction's authorization list — the
account's last applied one there.

blockNumber.description: Block of the transaction that carried the authorization.

txHash.description:
The hash of that transaction, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed. Absent when it could not be
resolved.

txIndex.description:
That transaction's position in its block. Equal to the frame's own block and
transaction when the transaction authorized the delegation itself: it is in force
from the transaction's first frame.

FunctionCalls.description: How often one function of an address was called.

candidateCount.description: How many known signatures share the selector. Absent when no lookup was made.

decodeStatus.description:
How confident the name is: `partial`, `ambiguous`, `abi_missing`. Absent when no lookup
was made.

kind.description:
`function` for a selector; `no_selector` for transactions received with fewer than 4
bytes of input — plain value transfers and short inputs alike, one entry.

lastTopLevelCallBlock.description: The block of the last of them.

name.description: The function name, when a known signature has this selector. Absent otherwise.

nameState.description:
`withheld` when a known signature has the selector but its text is not served: see
`RegistryNameState`. Absent otherwise.

signature.description:
The canonical signature, for example `transfer(address,uint256)`. Absent when no
known signature has this selector.

topLevelCalls.description: Transactions the address received with this selector — top-level calls only.

GasDaily.description: Gas prices and transaction types per day over a window of UTC dates.

days.description: One entry per day of the window, oldest first.

from.description: First day of the window, UTC date `YYYY-MM-DD`, included.

to.description: Last day of the window, UTC date `YYYY-MM-DD`, included.

GasDailyResponse.description: Response of a network daily method.

data.description: The answer itself: what this method returns, described by its own schema.

meta.description:
Response metadata: when it was produced, whether it came from the cache, the block it
is current as of where the method states one, and the link to its documentation.

GasDayOut.description: Gas prices and transaction types on one UTC day.

gasPriceAvgWei.description:
Average effective gas price paid, in wei, as a decimal string. Absent where it is
not available.

gasPriceMedianWei.description:
Median effective gas price paid, in wei, as a decimal string. Absent where it is not
available.

gasPriceP10Wei.description:
10th percentile of the effective gas price paid, in wei, as a decimal string. Absent
where it is not available.

gasPriceP90Wei.description:
90th percentile of the effective gas price paid, in wei, as a decimal string. Absent
where it is not available.

priorityFeeAvgWei.description:
Average priority fee (tip) paid per gas, in wei, as a decimal string. Absent where
it is not available.

priorityFeeMedianWei.description:
Median priority fee (tip) paid per gas, in wei, as a decimal string. Absent where it
is not available.

provisional.description: `true` for a day the source is still counting or may still revise.

HotSlotRow.description: One slot and how often it changed in the window.

changes.description: Blocks of the window in which its value changed.

IndexedDynamicHash.description:
An indexed dynamic argument (`string`, `bytes`, an array): the log carries only the
keccak-256 hash of its value, so the value itself cannot be recovered from the log.

dynamic.description: Always `true`: marks the value as the hash of a dynamic argument.

hash.description: keccak-256 of the argument's value, `0x` + 64 lowercase hex.

arg.description: The PUSH argument, `0x`-prefixed; absent for every other instruction.

inMetadata.description:
Present (`true`) only when a byte of the instruction lies inside the compiler's
metadata: data that decodes to instructions, not code that runs.

op.description: The mnemonic, for example `PUSH1` or `SSTORE`; `?` for a byte that is not an opcode.

pc.description: Byte offset of the instruction in the code.

truncated.description:
Present (`true`) only for a PUSH whose argument runs past the end of the code; `arg`
holds the bytes that exist.

Assets the address holds a positive balance of that could NOT be valued: no USD price
for the hour, the token's decimals are unknown, or the value is larger than the price
can vouch for — a price taken from a thin market, applied to an amount far beyond what
that market trades. Such a holding is unvalued, never valued at a capped amount.

together are everything held.

nextCursor.description:
Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last page. Pages walk the
valued positions as of `window.asOfBlock`. With `block`, that set is fixed and the
pages tile it exactly. Without `block`, the current set can be valued anew between two
pages (at most every few minutes, and at each new price hour); a cursor issued before
that is then refused with `invalid_cursor` — restart from the first page, or pass
`block` for a set that cannot move. A walk therefore never skips a position.

positions.description:
This page of the valued positions, in descending USD value (ties: the native asset
first, then by token address), at most `limit` rows. No NFTs, no DeFi positions, no
liquidity-pool shares — token balances and the native asset only.

latest hour a price was observed for its asset).

With `priceBasis: hour_of_block`: start of the UTC hour every position is priced at,

pricedCount.description: How many positions carry a USD value — the size of the whole set the pages walk.

totalUsd.description:
Sum of `valueUsd` over ALL valued positions of the address — not only the ones on this
page. Absent when nothing could be valued (absent, never 0).

asset). `balance` divided by `10^decimals` is the amount in whole units.

priceCarried.description:
`true` when no price was observed in that hour and the latest earlier price is used
instead.

priceHour.description: Start of the UTC hour `priceUsd` is for, Unix seconds.

priceUsd.description: USD price of one whole unit of the asset at `priceHour`.

symbol.description:
Ticker as declared by the token contract; `ETH` for the native asset. Absent when
the contract declares none. Not a proof of identity: any contract can declare any
symbol.
Absent when longer than 64 characters — left out whole, never shortened.

token.description: The token contract, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed. Absent for the native asset.

valueUsd.description:
`balance / 10^decimals * priceUsd`. A floating-point estimate; the exact value follows
from `balance` and `priceUsd`.

PositionKind.description: Kind of asset a portfolio position is.

PriceBasis.description: Which hour the USD prices of a portfolio are for.

Proof.description:
The evidence behind one proven fact — an attribute of an address, or a relation
between two addresses. Nothing here is summarised or ranked: the fields are the
evaluator's own record, so a reader can check the claim rather than trust it.

bindingVersions.description:
The data bindings the evaluation read, keyed by an opaque binding identifier
(`ev:` + 12 hex characters). Each value is the version of what the binding was
resolved to — a plain version such as `1.0.0` where the evaluator recorded one,
otherwise an opaque identifier of the resolved source. Both identifiers are stable:
the same binding, and the same source, carry the same identifier in every proof.
Absent when the record does not state the bindings in a readable form.

chainId.description: Chain id the fact is about. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

definitionVersion.description: Version of the definition the fact was evaluated against.

dependencyProofRefs.description:
Other proofs this one depends on, one entry per proof. Empty for a fact that rests
on no other proof; `null` when the record does not state them in a readable form.

evaluatedAt.description: When the evaluation ran, Unix time in seconds.

evaluatorVersion.description:
Version of the evaluator that produced this proof, e.g. `1.0.0`. A different value
on two proofs means they were produced by different evaluator releases.

oneOf.description:
The facts checked, each with its identifier (`fact_id`), the operator, the expected
and the observed value. Where a check names the evidence it read, that reference is
an opaque identifier (`ev:` + 12 hex characters), stable across proofs. `null` when
the record does not state the checks in a readable form.

failureReasonCodes.description:
Reason codes when `result` is not `pass`, each a `snake_case` string (for example
`coverage_unknown`). Empty on a passing fact; `null` when the record does not state
them in a readable form.

graphRevision.description:
Revision of the knowledge graph's rule set that produced this proof: an opaque
identifier, `rev:` + 12 hex characters. Stable — the same revision carries the same
identifier in every proof; compare it for equality, it has no order.

oneOf.description:
Conditions that had to be false for the fact to hold, each with its identifier
(`control_id`) and what was observed. `null` when the record does not state them in
a readable form.

object.description: The other end of a relation. Absent on an attribute proof.

proofHash.description: Digest of the proof record, `sha256:` + hex.

referenceBlock.description: Block the evidence was read at.

referenceBlockHash.description: Hash of that block, `0x`-prefixed — pins the evidence to one chain state.

result.description: Evaluation result. `pass` means the fact is proven.

selectedFamilyId.description: Which of the fact's alternative evidence families satisfied it.

snapshotId.description: Identifier of the chain snapshot the evaluation ran on.

sourceEvidenceRefs.description:
Where the evidence was read from: one entry per evidence source, each an opaque
identifier. Absent when the record does not state the sources in a readable form.

subject.description: The address the fact is about, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

value.description: The fact's value, for facts that carry one.

additionalProperties.description:
Any other key of the check, with its value: a number, a boolean, a plain value or an
opaque evidence identifier, or an object or a list of those.

ProofCheck.description:
One check of a proof. Its keys are written as the evaluation records them, in
`snake_case`; the ones below are the common ones, and a check may carry others. In any
key outside `fact_id`, `control_id`, `operator` and `evaluation`, a string is either a
plain value (a `0x` hex value or a number) or an opaque evidence identifier (`ev:` + 12
hex characters, stable across proofs).

control_id.description: The condition this check evaluates, on a negative control. Absent on a fact check.

evaluation.description: What a negative control requires of its observation, for example `must_be_false`.

expected.description:
The value the comparison expects, where the operator compares against one: a
boolean, a number or a string.

fact_id.description: The fact this check evaluates, on a fact check. Absent on a negative control.

observed.description: The value observed in the evidence: a boolean, a number or a string.

threshold.description:
The bound the comparison applies, where the operator takes one (for example the
minimum count of `exists`): a number, or a boolean or a string where the record
states one so.

ProofChecks.description:
The checks of a proof: the list of check records, or — where the record states a single
check — that one record.

oneOf.description: The check records, in the order they were evaluated.
A single check record.

ProofDependencyRef.description: A reference to another proof that this one depends on.

oneOf.description: An identifier of the proof depended on.

A record naming the proof depended on: its keys as the evaluation records them,
each value a scalar (strings are opaque evidence identifiers), an object or a list.

ProofResponse.description: Response of the two proof methods.

data.description: The answer itself: what this method returns, described by its own schema.

meta.description:
Response metadata: when it was produced, whether it came from the cache, the block it
is current as of where the method states one, and the link to its documentation.

ProtocolVolume.description: One protocol's DEX trading on one UTC day.

protocol.description: The protocol as the index names it (`uniswap`, `curve`, …).

unpricedPools.description: Active pools that could not be priced; absent when none. Present ⇒ `volumeUsd` is partial.

volumeUsd.description: USD volume over the pools that could be priced; absent when none could.

ProvenAt.description: A proven answer and the block it speaks about.

referenceBlock.description: The block the answer was evaluated at.

ProxyImplementation.description: One implementation a proxy has been observed delegating to, and whether it still does.

beacon.description:
Only on a `storage_beacon` row, where `implementation` is the BEACON: the logic
contracts the beacon handed to its proxies, read on the beacon itself. Absent on every
other row, and when the beacon's history could not be read.

firstSeenBlock.description: First block the pointer was observed at.

implementation.description:
The implementation address, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed. For a beacon proxy this is
the BEACON: the logic contract behind it is resolved on the beacon, not here.

isSelfDelegation.description: `true` when the proxy delegates to itself.

lastSeenBlock.description: Last block the pointer was observed at.

proxyFamily.description:
Pattern classification of the proxy contract, for example `eip1967_impl`, `beacon`,
`minimal_proxy`, `safe`; `none` or `unknown` when no pattern was recognised. The set
grows as patterns are added.

slot.description:
The storage slot the pointer was read from, `0x`-prefixed. Absent for
`eip1167`, where the pointer is in the code.

slotLastEvent.description:
The last write observed on the pointer's slot: `upgrade` (a new implementation
was written), `cleared` (the slot was emptied) or `unset` (the pointer was removed:
zero written), with the block and transaction. Absent when no write to the slot is
indexed.

source.description:
How the implementation was found: `eip1167` (minimal-proxy bytecode),
`storage_eip1967_impl` (the EIP-1967 implementation slot), `storage_beacon` (the
EIP-1967 beacon slot), `storage_oz_v1` (the OpenZeppelin v1 slot),
`storage_safe_singleton` (slot 0 of a Safe proxy: the singleton it delegates to).

supersededBy.description:
Whether this pointer has since been replaced. Three states, and each means something
different: ABSENT — storage cannot say (the pointer lives in the code, or on a
beacon upgraded elsewhere); `null` — no replacement observed, the pointer is current;
an address — the pointer was replaced by it.

supersededByBlock.description: Block of the replacement. Present exactly when `supersededBy` is an address.

ProxyImplementations.description: The implementations a proxy contract has delegated to.

address.description: The proxy contract address, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

chainId.description: Chain id the contract is on. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

implementations.description:
Newest-seen first. Empty when no implementation pointer has been observed for the
address — which is not a statement that it is not a proxy.

data.description: The answer itself: what this method returns, described by its own schema.

meta.description:
Response metadata: when it was produced, whether it came from the cache, the block it
is current as of where the method states one, and the link to its documentation.

asOfBlock.description:
The block height the answer is valid at — the same place on every method, whatever
the body's own shape. Absent when the method's source states no block (a ranking
recomputed daily, a set of proven facts): absence means "not stated", never
"latest".

cached.description:
`true` when the answer came from the TraceFast response cache rather than being
computed for this call. Cached answers are refreshed within minutes.

chain.description: Network the answer is about. `ethereum` for chain id `1`.

coverage.description:
Block heights that bound what this method can state, by name — for example the
first block from which a derived fact is computed, or the last block a lagging fact
has reached. Present only on methods whose coverage is bounded; each such method
documents its keys. Re-read on every call, so a cached body carries current bounds.

docs.description: Documentation page of the method that produced this response.

timestamp.description: When this response was produced, Unix time in milliseconds.

RankedPoolToken.description: One token of a ranked pool.

symbol.description:
The symbol the token contract declares — verbatim, not verified.
Absent when longer than 64 characters — left out whole, never shortened.

ReceivedCall.description: One transaction that called the address — directly or from inside another contract.

blockNumber.description: Height of the block that includes the transaction.

callTypes.description:
The kinds of those frames: `call` and `staticcall` (the address was called),
`delegatecall` and `callcode` (the address ran ANOTHER contract's code in its own
context, as a proxy does), `selfdestruct` (a self-destruct sent its balance here).
Other values may be added.

carriedValue.description: At least one of those frames carried ETH.

failedFrames.description: Of them, how many failed by themselves (reverted or halted).

frames.description:
How many call frames of the transaction ran in this address's context — on its own
storage and balance (counted up to 65 535). For a proxy this includes the frames in
which it ran its implementation's code, so one call to a proxy is often two frames.

timestamp.description: Block time, Unix seconds. Absent with `txHash`.

transactionTarget.description:
`true` when the address is the transaction's own target; `false` when it was called
only from inside other contracts.

txHash.description: The transaction's hash. Absent when it could not be resolved for this answer.

txIndex.description: Position of the transaction within its block, from `0`.

txSender.description:
The account that sent the transaction (not necessarily the direct caller: the call may
come from a contract it reached). Absent with `txHash`.

txSucceeded.description:
`false` when the transaction itself reverted: then nothing it did took effect, even if
`failedFrames` is 0 (a frame undone by its caller keeps its own success). Absent with
`txHash`.

RegistryNameState.description:
Why a known selector carries no `name` and no `signature`. `withheld`: a known signature
has this selector, but its text is not served — its name is not an identifier
(`[A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*`) of at most 128 characters, or its signature is not made of
identifier characters, commas, parentheses and brackets of at most 512. It is still
counted in `candidateCount` and `decodeStatus`; it is NOT `abi_missing` (no known
signature). Absent otherwise.

counterpart.description:
The other end of the relation, lowercase `0x`-prefixed: the object when `direction`
is `subject`, the subject when it is `object`.

referenceBlock.description: Block height at which the relation was evaluated.

result.description: Evaluation result. `pass` means the relation is proven.

value.description: The relation's value, for relations that carry one.

RelationCount.description: How many addresses point at one address under one relation id.

count.description: Addresses holding this relation towards the address, now.

RelationHistory.description: Every relation interval an address has held, in one direction, oldest first.

chainId.description: Chain id the facts are about. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

coveredFamilies.description:
Relation ids the history is built for. An empty or short timeline says nothing
about relations outside this list.

direction.description:
The side the address is read on, echoed: `subject` lists what it pointed at,
`object` lists who pointed at it.

intervals.description: Intervals in ascending order of `startBlock`, then relation id, then the other end.

nextCursor.description:
Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent on the last page. Pass it back unchanged
as `?cursor=`; a cursor is only valid for the request it was issued for.

total.description:
Number of intervals the address holds as the subject — the length of the whole
timeline under `direction=subject`. Absent under `direction=object`, which is not
counted.

truncated.description: `true` when the timeline was cut at `limit`; `nextCursor` continues it.

data.description: The answer itself: what this method returns, described by its own schema.

meta.description:
Response metadata: when it was produced, whether it came from the cache, the block it
is current as of where the method states one, and the link to its documentation.

RelationInterval.description: One relation and the block window it held for.

counterpart.description:
The other end of the relation, lowercase `0x`-prefixed: the object when the
address is the subject, the subject when the address is the object.

endBlock.description:
Last block the relation held at. Absent when the interval was still open at the
end of the covered history.

startBlock.description: First block the relation held at.

value.description: The relation's value over the interval, for relations that carry one.

Relations.description: One page of the relations an address holds now.

chainId.description: Chain id the facts are about. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

counts.description:
`direction=object`, first page only (no `cursor`): how many addresses point at this
one, per relation id, ordered by id; narrowed to `attributeId` when it is given.
Current as of the graph's latest hourly refresh — there is no single block for it,
it is a separate read from the page and may differ from it by one refresh, and
`meta.asOfBlock` does not describe it. An empty list means nothing proven points at
this address. Absent on the subject side and on later pages: not computed there,
never zero.

direction.description:
The side the address is read on, echoed: `subject` lists what it points at,
`object` lists who points at it.

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page. Absent on the last page. There is no single total.

relations.description: The page, ordered by relation id then counterpart.

RelationsAtBlock.description: The relations an address was the subject of at one block.

address.description:
The address, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed. Always the SUBJECT of the relations
listed: "what did this address point at".

addressKnown.description:
`false` when the address is unknown to the history altogether. Absent when the
history does not state it.

block.description: The block the question was asked about.

chainId.description: Chain id the facts are about. `1` is Ethereum mainnet.

coverageBlock.description: The highest block the history has been computed up to.

coveredFamilies.description:
Relation ids the history is built for. A relation outside this list is not listed
here whether or not it held.

intervals.description:
The relations that held at `block`, each with its window. `counterpart` is the
object of every relation here.

ReserveLegNow.description: One token of a pool's reserves.

decimals.description: The decimals the token contract declares. Absent when unknown.

pricingQuality.description: Whether the leg's price is trusted, as the source rates it.

pricingSource.description:
Where the leg's price came from: `observed`, `filled` (carried from an earlier hour)
or `none`.

reserve.description:
`reserveRaw` in whole token units (scaled by `decimals`) as a floating-point number
— an approximation for display; `reserveRaw` is exact. Absent when the decimals are
unknown.

reserveRaw.description:
The reserve as the raw integer, a decimal string (it may be negative where the source
reads a signed balance).

reserveUsd.description: Its USD value, where the token has a price trusted at that size.

symbol.description:
The symbol the token contract declares — verbatim, not verified. Absent when
unknown.
Absent when longer than 64 characters — left out whole, never shortened.

ResolveCorpus.description: A collection a text query is looked up in.

ResolveNameState.description:
Why a match carries no `name` although TraceFast shows one. `withheld_for_size`: the name
is longer than 256 characters and is not given (never cut). Absent otherwise — then a
missing `name` means the address is shown under no name.

ResolvedBlock.description: A block a number query resolved to. Pass `number` to the block methods.

ResolvedEntity.description: One address the query resolves to.

address.description: The address, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed. Pass it to the address methods.

impersonates.description:
The asset this address is flagged as imitating, by its symbol. Absent when it is not
flagged.

match.description:
How closely it matched: `exact`, `prefix`, `substring`, or `address_fragment`
(inside a symbol or name that carries an address-like hex string — often an
impersonation; ranked last).

matchedOn.description:
Where the query matched: `address` (the query is this address), `token_symbol`,
`token_name` (what the token contract declares) or `name` (the name TraceFast
shows).

name.description:
The name TraceFast shows for the address — a project, exchange or protocol name, an
ENS name, or the name a contract declares where it is shown. Absent when TraceFast
shows the address under no name, or when `nameState` is `withheld_for_size`.

nameStanding.description:
How TraceFast presents the address: `verified` (confirmed by an official source),
`normal`, `qualified` (shown with a qualifier, e.g. a name the contract declares
about itself), `warning`, `danger` (flagged — for example an impersonation or a
scam), or `unknown`. Other values may be added. Absent when TraceFast holds no
presentation for the address.

nameState.description:
`withheld_for_size` when TraceFast shows a name for the address but it is longer than
256 characters: `name` is absent — it is not "no name". Absent otherwise.

token.description: The token contract's own identity, when it is one.

type.description: What kind of address it is.

ResolvedToken.description: The token contract's identity as it declares it.

The name the contract declares — verbatim, not verified.

`found`: TraceFast indexes the address as a token contract, with the name and symbol
below. `absent`: no token metadata is recorded — not a statement that it is no
token. `unavailable`: could not be read for this answer.

symbol.description:

blockNumber.description: Height of the block that includes the transaction.

txIndex.description: Position of the transaction within its block, from `0`.

ResolvedType.description: What kind of address a match is: its proven type attributes.

attributes.description:
Proven attribute ids of the families `asset` (what it is as an asset, e.g.
`asset:fungible_token`), `address_nature` (e.g. `address_nature:contract_currently`)
and `derived:account_type` — the ones a type is read from; the full set is the
address-attributes method's. Present only when `state` is `known`.

state.description:
`known`: TraceFast has evaluated the address, and `attributes` lists its proven type
attributes (possibly none). `unknown`: not evaluated yet — nothing is denied.
`unavailable`: could not be read for this answer.

Selector.description: One function selector of a contract, resolved to a signature where one is known.

candidateCount.description:
How many known signatures share this selector. `1` is unambiguous; when several do,
`signature` is the most common one.

decodeStatus.description:
How confident the resolution is: `partial` (one known signature; parameter names
are not known), `ambiguous` (several known signatures share the selector),
`abi_missing` (no known signature).

name.description:
The function name alone. Present whenever the selector is named; it can be present
WITHOUT `signature` when the only known signature for it is malformed — the name is
served, the malformed text is not. A known name is served only as an identifier
(`[A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*`) of at most 128 characters, and a signature only in
identifier characters, commas, parentheses and brackets, of at most 512: anything else
in the registry is treated as unknown.

nameState.description:
`withheld` when a known signature has the selector but its text is not served: see
`RegistryNameState`. Absent otherwise.

signature.description:
The canonical signature, for example `transfer(address,uint256)`. Absent when no
known signature has this selector.

Signal.description:
One signal of a TraceFast detector: a fast hypothesis about what happened in a transaction,
never a fact about an address.

blockNumber.description: The block the signal is about.

blockTimestamp.description: Unix seconds of the block; absent when the detector did not state it.

callPath.description:
The call frame's position in the transaction's call tree (four hex characters per level,
as the trace methods write it), where the detector named a frame.

complete.description:
The detector read every input it needed. `false`: a value the evidence does not state
is unknown, not absent.

detector.description: The detector that raised it; its coverage is in getSignalRates.

evidence.description:
The evidence fields of the kind, as the detector wrote them (getSignalKinds lists them).
Addresses are `0x` + 40 hex; amounts in wei or raw token units are decimal strings.
Absent when the detector's evidence could not be read.

kind.description: The kind (getSignalKinds lists them with their evidence fields).

logIndexInTx.description: The event's index within the transaction, where the detector named an event.

signalId.description: The signal's own id (`0x` + 64 hex): stable across the detector's revisions of it.

slot.description: The storage slot of `subject` (`0x` + 64 hex), where the detector named one.

subject.description: The contract or account the signal is about.

txHash.description: The transaction; absent when the detector did not name one.

SignalKind.description: One kind served as a row by getSignals.

alwaysTrader.description: Always in the trader view. Other kinds are in it only about a traded token.

evidenceFields.description: The evidence fields the kind carries; `a.b` = only the field `b` of the object `a`.

kind.description: The kind's id, as the `kind` of a signal carries it.

countedKinds.description:
Kinds getSignalRates always counts, zero included. It also counts every other kind that
is not a row kind whenever one is raised (governance and timelock actions, sweeps, …).

detectors.description: Every detector getSignalRates states coverage for.

rowKinds.description: The kinds getSignals serves as rows (the values its `kind` filter takes).

SignalKindsResponse.description: Response of the signal kinds method.

flashLoans.description: Flash-loan transactions per class (`unstated` when the detector gave none).

toBlock.description: Last block of the window — the block the counts are true up to.

windowBlocks.description: Length of the window in blocks (7 200).

SlotEvent.description: One write to a proxy's pointer slot.

blockNumber.description: Block of the write.

kind.description:
`upgrade` — an implementation address was written to the slot (the first one
included); `cleared` — the slot was emptied; `unset` — zero was written, the pointer
removed.

txHash.description: Hash of the transaction that made the write, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

SlotKeyLayout.description: How the innermost hash of a `derived` key was built.

SlotMeaning.description: What a storage slot is. Numbers that can exceed 2^53 ride as decimal strings.

baseSlot.description:
`derived` only, when the chain of hashes was traced down to a small number: the slot of
the declared variable (the mapping or the array itself), decimal string.

chainOffsets.description:
`derived` only: the offsets of the hash chain's links, in declaration order as traced,
decimal strings. Which mapping key each offset goes with is not stated, and the two
lists can differ in length.

depth.description:
`derived` and `fixed_slot` only: how many levels of hashing were traced — `0` none
(`fixed_slot`: the key is not a hash), `1` one mapping or array, `2`-`3` nested ones. Absent
on the other kinds, where nothing was traced: absence there is not `0`.

kind.description:
`derived` | `fixed_slot` | `unknown` | `not_computed` | `before_coverage`. Treat a value
you do not recognise as "nothing known about the slot".

layout.description: `derived` only: how the innermost hash was built. Absent when it cannot be told.

layoutAmbiguous.description:
`derived` only: `true` when both words of the innermost hash are small numbers, so which
one is the key and which the slot cannot be told apart; the Solidity order is assumed.
Absent on the other kinds, which have no hash to read.

mappingKeys.description:
`derived` only: the mapping keys found in the hash chain, in declaration order as
traced, as `0x`-prefixed 32-byte words (64 lowercase hex characters; an address is
left-padded with zeros). An array level uses no key, so there can be fewer keys than
`depth`; which level each key belongs to is not stated. Absent when a key could not be
read as a 32-byte word — the list is never served in part.

offset.description:
`derived` only: the offset added to the hash, a struct member or an array element
inside the mapped value, decimal string. Absent when not traced.

slot.description: `fixed_slot` only: the key's own value, decimal string.

variableIdentified.description:
`derived` only: `true` when the chain of hashes ends at a small base slot — the variable
is identified (`baseSlot`). Absent on the other kinds: a `fixed_slot` is not
necessarily a declared variable, and on `unknown` / `not_computed` / `before_coverage`
nothing was traced, so `false` there would be a claim nobody computed.

SlotMeaningKind.description: How a storage slot's key was computed, as far as it could be traced.

SlotValueChange.description: One block in which the slot's value changed.

blockNumber.description: The block in which the slot's value changed.

valueAfter.description:
The value after the block. Absent when it is not stated (the newest change) — never a
zero standing in.

valueBefore.description: The value before the block, `0x` + 64 hex.

writerTxs.description:
Every transaction that wrote the slot in this block, by position — writes of the value
it already held included. Empty for a system write with no transaction; absent while the
block is not attributed yet.

SlotWriterTx.description: A transaction that wrote the slot.

txHash.description: Hash of the writing transaction, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

txIndex.description: Position of the writing transaction within its block, from `0`.

StateDependency.description:
One read-after-write edge inside a block: `readerTxIndex` read the slot whose last
committed write before it, in this block, was `writerTxIndex`'s.

readerTxHash.description:
Hash of the reading transaction, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed. Absent when it could
not be resolved.

readerTxIndex.description: Position in the block of the transaction that read the slot.

role.description:
The asked transaction's side: `reader` (it read what an earlier one wrote) or
`writer` (a later one read what it wrote).

storageAddress.description: The contract whose slot carries the dependency, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

writerTxHash.description:
Hash of the writing transaction, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed. Absent when it could
not be resolved.

writerTxIndex.description: Position in the block of the transaction whose write was read.

StateDependencyPair.description: One pair of dependent transactions, all their shared slots counted.

readerTxHash.description:
Hash of the reading transaction, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed. Absent when it could
not be resolved.

readerTxIndex.description: Position in the block of the transaction that read.

role.description:
The asked transaction's side: `reader` (it read what the other wrote) or `writer`
(the other read what it wrote).

storageAddresses.description: Distinct contracts those slots belong to.

writerTxHash.description:
Hash of the writing transaction, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed. Absent when it could
not be resolved.

writerTxIndex.description: Position in the block of the transaction whose writes were read.

sloadOpcodeTotal.description: SLOAD opcodes executed, reverted frames included.

sloadSlotTouches.description: Distinct slots read per transaction, summed over the day.

sstoreOpcodeTotal.description: SSTORE opcodes executed, reverted frames included.

sstoreSlotTouches.description: Distinct slots written per transaction, summed over the day.

txsReadOnly.description: Transactions that read the contract's storage without writing it.

txsReading.description: Transactions that read the contract's storage.

txsTouching.description: Transactions that touched the contract's storage (read or wrote it).

txsWriting.description: Transactions that wrote the contract's storage.

changes.description: Blocks in which its value changed.

currentValue.description: The current value, `0x` + 64 hex — only when `currentValueStatus` is `observed`.

currentValueStatus.description:
`observed`, `system_writes`, `ambiguous_order`, `storage_cleared`,
`no_transaction_write` or `not_computed`. Other values may be added.

firstChangeBlock.description: First block in which the slot's value changed.

lastChangeBlock.description: Last block in which the slot's value changed.

StorageSlot.description: One storage slot a transaction wrote.

meaning.description:
What the slot is: how its key was computed. Absent when no answer could be had for this
slot in this response — absence says nothing about the slot; ask again later.

storageAddress.description: The contract whose storage the slot is, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

writeCount.description:
How many times the transaction wrote this slot; within the first 5 000 writes of the
transaction when `slotsTruncated` is true.

StorageWrite.description: One storage slot written by one call frame of a transaction.

callDepth.description: Depth of the writing frame; `1` is the top-level call.

callPath.description:
The writing frame's address in the call tree — the same `callPath` the trace
methods use. Absent when the frame was not recorded.

callerAddress.description: The caller of the frame that executed the write, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

executionAddress.description:
The address whose code executed the write. It differs from `storageAddress` in a
`delegatecall`, where the code of an implementation writes the caller's storage.

storageAddress.description: The contract whose storage was written.

valueBefore.description:
The value the slot held before this write, 32 bytes. Present only when
`valueBeforeStatus` is `resolved`. A value of all zeroes is a real zero — the slot had
never been written, or had been cleared — not a filler.

valueBeforeStatus.description:
What can be said about the value before: `resolved` (present, and this write's own);
`not_derivable` (it cannot be established for this write and never will be — the
order of writes is not recorded for this block, or the slot is rewritten by a system
call after the transaction); or `not_computed` (the prior value has not been computed
for this write yet — not a statement that the slot was empty. This method refuses a
transaction above the writes' reach with 422 `coverage_gap`, so that is what a caller
normally meets instead).

writeIndex.description:
The execution ordinal of this write within the transaction, where recorded. Writes
are listed in this order; numbers may skip (writes undone by a reverted call are not
listed).

writeIndexStatus.description:
`present`, or `not_recorded` — the order of writes is not known for this block
(blocks below 2675000), which is not the same as "this was write 0".

StorageWriterRow.description: One (caller, execution address) pair that wrote the storage.

callerAddress.description: Who called the frame that wrote.

executionAddress.description: Whose code ran in that frame — the contract itself, or an implementation it delegated to.

firstBlock.description: First block this pair wrote in.

lastBlock.description: Last block this pair wrote in.

uniqueTxs.description: Distinct transactions they happened in — an estimate on large contracts.

Surface.description: Where an interaction can be observed.

Token.description: One token contract, as it declares itself.

decimals.description:
`decimals()` as declared. Absent when the contract declares none (NFTs, and some
fungible tokens) — absent, never a default of 18.

holderCount.description:
Number of addresses holding a positive balance now — the same number the holders
method states. Absent when holders are not covered for this token (every NFT
collection today) — absent, never zero.

holderCountAllTime.description:
Number of distinct addresses that have EVER held the token, including those holding
nothing now. Absent where it is not available for this token.

name.description:
`name()` as the contract declares it — verbatim, not verified: a contract may
declare any text. Absent when the contract declares none.
Absent when longer than 128 characters — left out whole, never shortened.

standard.description:
Token standard as observed from its events: `erc20`, `erc721`, `erc1155`, `erc777`
or `erc4626`; `native` for the chain's own coin.

symbol.description:
`symbol()` as the contract declares it — verbatim, not verified: a contract may
declare any text. Absent when the contract declares none.
Absent when longer than 64 characters — left out whole, never shortened.

TokenBalance.description: The balance of one token on one address.

balance.description:
The balance in the token's smallest unit, as a decimal string. `"0"` is a real zero:
the token is covered and the address holds none of it at `window.asOfBlock`. A token
that is not covered is refused (`token_not_covered`), and a past block with no
recorded balance for the pair is refused too (`balance_not_available`) — never
answered with zero.

decimals.description: Decimals as declared by the token contract; absent when unknown.

symbol.description:
Ticker as declared by the token contract; absent when it declares none. Not a proof
of identity.
Absent when longer than 64 characters — left out whole, never shortened.

window.description: The block the balance is true at.

TokenDexVolume.description: A token's daily DEX volume over a window, oldest first.

totalSwaps.description: Swaps over the window. Absent when no day is recorded (not the same as zero).

totalVolumeUsd.description:
The USD volume over the window; partial when `unpricedDays` is present. Absent when no
day could be priced.

unpricedDays.description: Days with swaps but no USD price. Absent when there are none.

TokenDexVolumeDay.description: One UTC day of a token's DEX trading.

swapsAsToken0.description:
Swaps in pools where the token is the pair's first token (`token0`) — the pair
position, not a buy or sell direction.

swapsAsToken1.description:
Swaps in pools where the token is the pair's second token (`token1`) — the pair
position, not a buy or sell direction.

volumeUsd.description: USD volume; absent when the day's swaps could not be priced.

data.description: The answer itself: what this method returns, described by its own schema.

meta.description:
Response metadata: when it was produced, whether it came from the cache, the block it

balance.description:
The balance in the token's smallest unit, as a decimal string (not divided by
`decimals`).

TokenHolders.description: The largest current holders of a token.

asOfBlock.description:
The block the ranking is valid at: balances are counted up to it. Absent when it cannot
be stated — the ranking was being recomputed during the read — never "latest".

holderCount.description:
Number of addresses holding a positive balance now — the size of the set this list
is the top of. Holders who once held and now hold nothing are not counted.

holders.description:
Holders in descending balance order (ties by address), at most `limit` rows. No rank
number: balances can tie, and the order is all the data supports.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last page of the ranking.

rankingDepth.description:
How many holders the pageable ranking holds: following `nextCursor` serves exactly
these, in order. At most 1 000.

rankingTruncated.description:
`true` when holders rank below the last of the `rankingDepth` that no page serves — the
walk ends at the depth, not at `holderCount`; `false` when the ranking holds every
holder. A ranking shorter than 1 000 is every holder; a ranking of exactly 1 000 is
compared with `holderCount`, which is counted separately and can differ from it by a few
holders around a recomputation.

TraceFrame.description: One executed call frame of a transaction.

callPath.description:
The frame's address in the call tree, as TraceFast encodes it: four hex characters
per level, the root frame is `0000`.

childIndex.description:
The frame's position among the frames called by the same parent, from `0`, in the
order the parent made the calls: `0` is the parent's first call. The top-level call
has no siblings and is `0`. Equal to the last four hex characters of `callPath`.

codeAddress.description:
The address whose code this frame runs. On a `delegatecall` this is the
implementation while `to` stays the storage context — the PAIR is what makes a
proxy call readable, which is why `to` does not change meaning. When this address is
an account with an EIP-7702 delegation, the code that ran is its delegate's:
`executedCodeAddress`. Absent where there is no callee code (`create`, `create2`,
`selfdestruct`).

decodedCall.description:
The frame's decoded call. A nested frame's is decoded from `inputHead`: in full when
the head is the whole calldata, otherwise from the head only (`byteCoverage: head`).
The root frame's (depth 1) is decoded from the transaction's whole calldata exactly as
`get_transaction` decodes it — the same status, signature and values; a value too
large for a trace is `withheld_for_size`. Present wherever `inputHead` is served.

delegation.description:
The authorization that set that delegation. Present exactly when
`executedCodeAddress` is.

depth.description:
Depth in the tree; `1` is the top-level call — the only frame at depth `1`, so
`depth == 1` is how to recognise it.

errorSelector.description: The custom error's 4-byte selector — the ERROR selector, not `inputSelector`.

executedCodeAddress.description:
The code that actually ran when `codeAddress` is an account with an EIP-7702
delegation in force at this frame: the delegate the account points at. Present only on
such frames. Where the response's `delegatedCode.status` is `resolved`, a frame without
it ran its own code; while it is `pending`, absence says nothing yet.

from.description: The caller of the frame, lowercase and `0x`-prefixed.

gas.description: Gas offered to the frame, as a decimal string.

gasUsed.description: Gas the frame consumed, as a decimal string.

initCodeHash.description:
keccak-256 of the init code, `0x`-prefixed. Present only on a creating frame
(`create`, `create2`).

inputHead.description:
The first 260 bytes of the frame's calldata, `0x`-hex. Present when calldata heads
are included: always on the paged frames, and on the whole trace when
`includeCalldata` is true.

inputSize.description:
Full length of the frame's calldata in BYTES. Compare it against 260, not against
the hex string's length: the units differ. Present with `inputHead`.

inputTruncated.description:
`true` when `inputHead` is shorter than the frame's calldata (`inputSize` is larger
than the head's length in bytes): the head is the first bytes only. Present exactly
when `inputHead` is.

order.description:
Position in pre-order traversal of the call tree; `0` is the transaction's own
top-level call.

outputHead.description: The first 260 bytes of the frame's output, `0x`-hex. Present with `inputHead`.

outputSize.description:
Full length of the frame's output in BYTES. Compare it against 260, not against the
hex string's length. Present with `inputHead`.

parentPath.description: The `callPath` of the frame that made this call. Absent on the root frame.

revertData.description:
The raw ABI revert payload, `0x`-prefixed hex. It may be truncated —
`revertDataTruncated` says when, and a clipped payload decodes into a plausible but
wrong argument list, so check the flag before decoding. Absent when there is no
payload to state.

revertDataSize.description:
Full length of the revert payload in BYTES, whether or not `revertData` is
truncated. Absent with `revertData`.

revertDataTruncated.description:
`true` when `revertData` is shorter than the payload (`revertDataSize`). Absent with
`revertData`.

revertDecodeSource.description:
How `revertReason` was found. Present only when `revertDecodeStatus` is `decoded`.
`standard`: decoded from the revert payload itself — a standard `Error(string)` message or
a `Panic(uint256)` code. `registry`: a custom error — `revertReason` is the error's name,
found by its 4-byte selector (`errorSelector`) among known error signatures; its arguments
are not decoded (read them from `revertData`).

revertDecodeStatus.description:
Why `revertReason` is what it is: `decoded`, `undecodable` (a payload is present
but no name was found) or `absent` (no payload to decode). An empty reason is
ambiguous three ways, and this field is what separates them.

Named apart from the event decoder's `decodeStatus` on purpose: that vocabulary
describes event-decode confidence and the two appear in one response.

revertReason.description: The decoded revert reason, or the custom error's name when its selector is known.

salt.description: The `create2` salt, 32 bytes, `0x`-prefixed. Present only on a `create2` frame.

selfdestructBeneficiary.description: Who received the balance of a `selfdestruct` frame.

status.description:
`success`, `reverted` or `halted` — the FRAME's own outcome, which on a caught
revert differs from the transaction's.

to.description: The frame's target. Absent on a contract creation.

valueWei.description: Value this frame moved, in wei, as a decimal string.

Transaction.description: One transaction as recorded on chain, with its receipt's outcome.

blockNumber.description: Height of the block that includes the transaction.

effectiveGasPrice.description:
The price actually paid per gas, in wei, as a decimal string. Absent only while the
block's base fee is not yet available.

gasLimit.description: Gas limit the sender set, as a decimal string.

gasPrice.description:
`gasPrice` as declared, in wei, as a decimal string. Present on the types that carry
it (legacy and EIP-2930); absent otherwise.

gasUsed.description: Gas the transaction used, from its receipt, as a decimal string.

hasSelfdestruct.description: Whether a frame ran SELFDESTRUCT. Absent until the trace is computed.

inputSize.description: Size of the input in bytes.

internalTransfersCount.description:
Value transfers made by inner calls, from the call trace. Absent until the trace is
computed (usually within minutes); `0` is a fact.

logCount.description:
Number of receipt logs. Absent where not yet recorded; a log-less transaction is
an honest `0`.

maxFeePerGas.description:
`maxFeePerGas` as declared, in wei, as a decimal string. Present on EIP-1559 and
later types; absent on the types that do not carry it.

maxPriorityFeePerGas.description:
`maxPriorityFeePerGas` (the most the sender pays as a tip), in wei, as a decimal
string. Present on EIP-1559 and later types; absent on the types that do not carry

methodId.description:
The first four bytes of the input (`0x`-prefixed), when the input is at least four

methodName.description:
The called function's name, when its selector is in TraceFast's signature registry
(e.g. `transfer`). Absent when unknown, and when the registry's name is not an
identifier (`[A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*`) of at most 128 characters.

revert.description:
Why the transaction failed at the top level. Present on a failed transaction once
the trace is computed. Absent otherwise.

revertsTotal.description:
Call frames that reverted, at any depth, from the call trace. A successful
transaction can contain some. Absent until the trace is computed.

status.description:
Receipt status: `1` success, `0` failure. Absent when the receipt is not yet
available — absence is "unknown", never "failed".

storage.description:
What the transaction wrote to contract storage. Absent until the storage writes of
its block are computed: a missing block here is "not known yet", never "no writes".

timestamp.description: Unix time of the block, seconds.

to.description: Recipient. Absent for a contract creation.

txType.description: Transaction type (0 legacy, 1 EIP-2930, 2 EIP-1559, 3 EIP-4844, 4 EIP-7702).

TransactionAccountChanges.description:
Every account one transaction changed, with its balance, nonce and code before and after.

Three rules are the source's: the fee recipient has no row when its only change is the
priority fee (so "no row for the fee recipient" does not mean "it did not change"); an
account created and destroyed within the transaction has no row (no net change); the set
is never empty for a computed transaction (its sender always changes).

truncated.description: More accounts than the cap (5 000): these are the first ones by address.

tokenTransfers.description:

list is a statement: the transaction moved no token. Labels and names from any
resolver are not part of it.

Only with `includeTokenTransfers=true`: whether `tokenTransfers` lists every token
transfer the transaction emitted (`complete`), only the first ones (`truncated`), or
none because they cannot be read right now (`not_available`). Absent otherwise.

info.description: Read-only Ethereum facts from the TraceFast knowledge graph and live chain data: address attributes, top counterparties, token holders, address portfolios and token balances, now or at a past block; blocks and their transactions; a transaction, why it reverted and the events it emitted; a token contract's declared metadata; an address's transactions, token transfers and internal transfers; and the call frames a transaction executed. Every method takes the chain id in the path (`1`, Ethereum mainnet), answers in a `data` / `meta` envelope, and refuses in `{ "error": { "code", "message" } }`. A fact that is absent is not proven; absence never means the opposite. Every data method requires an API key in the `x-api-key` request header; this document itself needs none, which is why it can be linked from a public page. Every operation carries `x-minimum-plan`: the id of the cheapest TraceFast plan that includes it — one of `data` (Enriched Data), `intelligence`, `investigation` — and every plan above it includes it too; the plans and their prices are at https://tracefast.xyz/pricing.

get.description: TraceFast live Ethereum data: the last block whose time is at or before a Unix time, and the first block after it — the bracket around the moment. Block times rise strictly with the number, so the answer is exact. `final: false` means the time is after the newest block: a later block may still land at or before it, so ask again later; `nextBlock` is then absent. If blocks around the time are temporarily unavailable, the method answers `422 coverage_gap` rather than a pair across the gap. Pass a block's number to the block methods for its contents.

get.description: TraceFast live Ethereum data: every account whose own state — native balance, nonce or code — changed in one block, with what changed and the balance before and after, in address order. Accounts only mentioned by the block's activity without a state change are not listed. Paged by an opaque cursor: pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` until it is absent. Account changes are served to the chain head: a block with no account change answers an empty list, which is a statement about that block and not a gap. A block above the chain head does not exist yet and answers 404.

get.description: TraceFast live Ethereum data: every EIP-7702 authorization-list entry carried by the transactions of one block — the delegation target, the account that signed it (`authority`), the chain id and nonce it was signed for, the signature, and the carrying transaction's hash and position — in transaction order and then list order. `authorityStatus` says whether the signer is known: `recovered`, `recovery_failed` (an invalid signature — the authorization has no signer) or `not_available` (not determined yet). Empty when the block carries no type-4 transaction. Paged by an opaque cursor: pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` until it is absent. A block the authorization history has not reached yet answers 422 with the highest block it can answer; a block above the chain head does not exist yet and answers 404.

get.description: TraceFast knowledge graph: the addresses one address has INTERACTED with most, ranked by successful transactions. An interaction is any of three: a top-level transaction between the two, whether or not it carried ETH (so a contract the address called, such as a token contract it sent `transfer` to, is listed as a counterparty); an internal ETH transfer; or a token `Transfer` event naming both. Token events are counted as emitted: they are not checked against a balance change and zero amounts are included, so events planted by address-poisoning contracts appear as interactions. `sentTxCount` counts transactions in which the address is the sending side of such an interaction, not transactions it signed. A counterparty here is not proof that value moved between the two. Returns up to `limit` counterparties in ranking order, each with its transaction counts, first and last block of interaction, the surfaces the relation was seen on and the token classes involved, plus `corpus` — how many counterparties the ranking covered. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` to continue past the first page: the ranking holds `rankingDepth` counterparties (at most 1 000; 100 for the largest addresses), and `rankingTruncated` says whether more rank below them. Pages are cut from one ranking; when it is recomputed between two pages a cursor from before is refused with `invalid_cursor` (restart from the first page) — for a window that can happen after about 2 minutes, all-time and past-block cursors last longer. The zero address and the address itself are never ranked. `window=24h` or `7d` ranks the rolling last 24 hours or 7 days instead of the whole history. With `block`, the ranking as it stood at the end of that block, reconstructed from the full history up to it. Very large addresses are refused for a past block or a window with the bound stated, never answered with a narrowed set. With `counterparty`, the figures of that one pair in the same form (all-time, window or block), or `lookup.found: false`: read from the relationship graph, which for the largest addresses is not the daily top list their ranking comes from, so a pair can be newer than its ranking row; `lookup.excludedFromRanking` marks the zero address and the address itself. At a past block the pair is admitted by the same bounds as the ranking.

get.summary: Internal transfers of an address

get.description: TraceFast live Ethereum data: everything an address holds, valued in USD — its token balances and its native ETH, each with the balance, the hourly USD price, the USD value and the share of the total. Positions come in descending USD value, up to `limit` per page; pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` until it is absent to walk every valued position. `totalUsd`, `pricedCount` and `hiddenCount` are over the whole holding on every page. Pages are over the set as of `window.asOfBlock`: with `block` that set is fixed; without it, the current set can be valued anew between two pages, and a cursor from before that is refused with `invalid_cursor` (restart from the first page). A position is listed only when it can be valued (a USD price for the hour, known decimals, and a value within what that price can vouch for — a thin-market price is not applied to an amount far beyond what its market trades); anything else the address holds is counted in `hiddenCount`, never listed. Token balances are served for the covered tokens (`coveredTokenCount`, growing continuously); a balance in a token outside that set is absent, not zero. No NFTs, no DeFi positions, no liquidity-pool shares. With `block`, the exact state at the end of that block, priced at that block's hour.

get.description: TraceFast live Ethereum data: what a reference means. An address (`0x` + 40 hex) is described — the name TraceFast shows for it, how it presents it, what kind of address it is, its token identity. Any other text is looked up in two collections — token contracts by the symbol and name they declare, and the names TraceFast shows for projects, exchanges, protocols and ENS names — and answered with the matching addresses, best first: verified addresses, then the projects and ENS names TraceFast knows by name (flagged ones included), then the rest, and impersonations last — never hidden; inside each group exact, then prefix, then substring matches, then tokens with more holders. The starting point when you have a name and need an address. No cursor: `hasMore` says when a more specific query or a larger `limit` would show more (also when the matches carry long texts: the list is bounded in bytes); a shown name longer than 256 characters is withheld (`nameState: withheld_for_size`), not absent. A 32-byte hash (`queryKind: hash`) is looked up as a TRANSACTION and answered in `transaction` (a block hash is not resolved — look a block up by its number); a whole number is also stated as `block` when that block exists, beside the text matches.

A detector that has not covered a block cannot raise a signal in it: read its coverage with getSignalRates before reading an empty page as quiet. Paged by an opaque cursor: pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` until it is absent.

get.description: TraceFast live Ethereum data: the event logs a transaction emitted, in emission order, each with the emitting contract, topics and data, and — when the event signature is known — the decoded event name and arguments with a stated confidence. Decoding covers the common token, DeFi and protocol events; an unknown signature is returned raw with `decodeStatus: abi_missing`, and a known one whose layout does not fit the log with `failed` — raw as well, without `decoded`. When more than one known signature fits a log, the readings are listed — at most 8, `candidateCount` is the true count. One event's readings are bounded in size: a value too large to include is `valueState: withheld_for_size`, without `value`; a decoding stopped by its work budget before every known signature was tried says `decodeSearch: incomplete` — `ambiguous` with a reading, no `decodeStatus` without one, never `failed`. A log whose data is longer than 49 151 bytes comes without `data` — `dataState: withheld_for_size` and `dataLength` (bytes) instead; the topics and the decoding are still given. Each event names the call frame that emitted it (`callPath`, `callDepth`), the same path as in the transaction's trace, where that is known; `meta.coverage.eventAttributionFromBlock` names the first block from which it is computed. Paged by an opaque cursor; a page holds at most `limit` logs and may hold fewer when their `data` is large — the page is bounded by size, a log is never cut. A hash that is not known answers 404.
